qs.q: A patient with a defect in the sodium-potassium pump in the red blood cells has hemolytic anemia. What is the primary cellular consequence?
o: Shrinkage and crenation of red cells
Increased rigidity of the red cell membrane
Reduced deformability of red blood cells
Swelling and subsequent lysis of red cells
qs.e: Failure of the Na+/K+ pump leads to sodium and water influx, causing the red blood cells to swell and eventually lyse.
